newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end up, electronics surge.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end up, electronics surge.

text.p: Singapore shares ended firmer on Friday with electronic stocks leading gainers.

"Electronics have really done very well this year. They are mostly small cap stocks and it looks like that they will perform better than the big cap stocks where the earnings growth is expected to be quite flat," said a local fund manager.

The SES electronics index tounched a new year high of 134.26 before ending slightly lower at 133.96, up 2.21 percent. Among the top gainers were Creative, which surged S$2.40 (US$1.67) to S$28.60, Wong's Circuits, up 12 cents to US$1.75, and Sunright which ended 14 cents higher at S$2.20.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrial Index ended up 6.83 points at 2,066.21. Total market volume was an active 225.2 million shares with 166 gainers against 186 losers.
Newly-listed bookseller Popular Holdings topped the actives with over 55 million shares traded. It ended at S$0.52, up 44 percent over its initial offer price of S$0.36.

HongKong Land was also active rising 15 cents to US$2.58 following sharp gains in the Hong Kong stock market. Other gainers included Singapore Telecom, OUB foreign and DBS foreign. Vickers Ballas went ex-bonus and ended flat at S$1.25.
